body.q: At the year end, a business has paid $1 200 for insurance covering 12 months from 1 October. The financial year ends on 31 December. What is the amount of prepaid insurance at 31 December?
body.why: Nine of the twelve months (January to September) fall in the next year, so 9/12 × $1 200 = $900 is prepaid.

body.q: A business has accrued expenses of $450 for electricity at the year end. How is this shown in the statement of financial position?
body.why: Accrued expenses are amounts owed at the year end and are therefore current liabilities.

body.q: Rent paid during the year was $6 000. Rent prepaid at the end of the year was $500. What is the rent expense shown in the income statement?
body.why: Prepaid rent relates to the next year, so it is deducted: $6 000 - $500 = $5 500.

body.q: A business has a trade receivables balance of $20 000 and wants to create a allowance for doubtful debts of 5%. There was no previous allowance. What is the entry in the income statement?
body.why: 5% × $20 000 = $1 000, and creating a new allowance is recorded as an expense.

o: Reduction in expenses (or increase in profit) of $150
body.q: The allowance for doubtful debts was $800 at the start of the year. At the end of the year it is calculated as $650. How is the change treated in the income statement?
body.why: The allowance has decreased by $150, so too much was previously charged and the difference increases profit.

body.q: A machine cost $40 000 and is depreciated at 20% per year using the reducing balance method. What is the depreciation charge for the second year?
body.why: Year 1 is $8 000, leaving a net book value of $32 000, and 20% of $32 000 = $6 400.

body.q: A vehicle cost $25 000 and has an expected residual value of $5 000 after 5 years. What is the annual depreciation charge using the straight-line method?
body.why: Straight-line depreciation is (cost - residual value) ÷ useful life = $20 000 ÷ 5 = $4 000.

o: Rent receivable not yet received for the final month
Commission received for the following year
Interest owed by a bank but not yet paid
Fees owed by a customer for services already provided
body.q: Which of the following is an example of income received in advance at the year end?
body.why: Income received in advance is cash received during the year that relates to a future period, such as commission for next year.

body.q: A business has wages of $18 000 paid during the year. At the year end, $1 500 of wages is owing. What is the wages expense for the year?
body.why: Owing wages are added to the amount paid: $18 000 + $1 500 = $19 500.

o: To increase the profit for the year
To follow the matching concept so that expenses are matched with the period in which they were incurred
To reduce the amount of tax payable
To make sure the trial balance totals agree
body.q: Why does a business make adjustments for accruals and prepayments before preparing its final accounts?
body.why: Adjustments apply the matching concept so that income and expenses are recorded in the period they relate to, regardless of when cash is paid or received.
